title: Decision sufficiency of empirical fixed-point representations in two JSSP search implementations
scope: Finite empirical replication. No new FP mechanism, no changes to old results.
instance_origin: Newly generated classical permutation-route JSSP: independent uniform machine permutation per job, integer durations Uniform{1,...,99}. These are synthetic research instances, not new public benchmark records, not a claim of distribution shift.

second_solver.window: Up to eight accepted moves, full sweeps, natural stopping. Unequal evaluations and seconds explicitly retained; not equal computational work.

original_solver.mode: Frozen old model transfer; no refitting on new final results
original_solver.settings: Original 180 generations, population80,9 atomic checkpoints,5repeats; secondary480 requests at generations40/100/160;20finalseeds

second_solver_models.dynamics: Existing affine displacement ridge, raw normal-equation penalty0.1, separate action maps and pooled baseline. Fit training transitions averaged over repeats. No new FP family.
second_solver_models.scorer: One action-interacted standardized ridge expected-gain regressor, sum squared error plus coefficient L2=1; intercept unpenalized; normal-equation gradient absolute max<=1e-7. Same scorer and optimizer in A-E.
second_solver_models.secondary_scorer: Same representations with existing converged logistic event scorer, L2=1, gradient tolerance1e-7; secondary only. No target choice by outcomes.
second_solver_models.B: A + structural5 + all upper-triangle degree2 products of dynamics4 (10 terms)
second_solver_models.C: B + action-conditioned predicted endpoint coordinates (12 terms), same transition supervision as FP
second_solver_models.D: B + norms of action displacements (3) and all pairwise predicted endpoint differences (3), Euclidean norm on the four dimensionless coordinates
second_solver_models.E: B + action-conditioned displacement coordinates (12), their coordinate squares(12), all pairwise prediction-difference coordinates(12), their squares(12). Direct expected-gain NoFP, same transition maps/supervision/history; greater expressiveness explicitly disclosed, no claim of identical capacity.
second_solver_models.negative_control: D_random: six fixed random affine norms of dynamics4, same added width as D; seeded before fitting
second_solver_models.train: Development8 only. Leave-one-development-instance-out transition features for scorer training. Full-development maps for held-out prediction; no final labels.
second_solver_models.validation: Four disjoint synthetic instances, interface/numerical validity only. No model/threshold/hyperparameter selection.
second_solver_models.oracle: Choose with repeats0,1, evaluate independently on repeats2,3,4. Reverse split secondary. Same-repeat sample maximum is explicitly optimistic, never true oracle.
second_solver_models.decision_loss: Only independent-repeat proxy regret and realized cross-instance policy value estimable; do not claim identification of V(S) or irreducible representation loss.

statistics.primary_endpoint: Instance-mean normalized offline selected improvement (start best minus endpoint best)/initial makespan, equal weighting of seeds and opportunities
statistics.test: Exact two-sided instance-level signed-rank, Holm across3;20000 instance cluster bootstrap draws, seed2026102502;95percentileCI
statistics.secondary: AP/Brier separate per-action event discrimination; within-state pairwise ranking; state RMSE against identity/pooled; action changes; independent-repeat sample-winner optimism; cost; no secondary promoted to primary
statistics.gate_online: Both second-solver primary comparisons positive mean,95CI lower>0,Holm p<.05 and every leave-one-instance-out mean>0. Old-solver transfer must also establish benefit for any cross-solver online claim. Otherwise no online FP deployment.
statistics.null: Failure to reject is not equivalence; no general claim beyond these solvers, sizes and generator.

failure_rules: No outcome-based dropping/rerunning/replacing instances or seeds. Malformed or incomplete cell aborts dependent confirmation. All unsuccessful cells retained. Engineering-only fixes documented with before/after hashes. Final collection only after code/model lock.

hypotheses.H1: State-error improvement does not imply positive within-state action ranking or selected reward. Counterexample to a universal dissociation would be consistently aligned improvements, but this finite study cannot prove universal implication either way.
hypotheses.H2: For a fitted map fixed independently of test outcomes, F=f_D(Z) implies sigma(Z,F,D)=sigma(Z,D); ideal conditional value unchanged. Learned finite-class policies may differ. If F uses omitted historical observations, antecedent is false.
hypotheses.H3: Split-repeat optimism and within-state reward variation quantify part of the prediction/decision mismatch; no unidentifiable noise-vs-information decomposition claimed.
hypotheses.H4: Test direction and scope independently in a second machine-order/tabu implementation, not merely GA parameter variation.
hypotheses.H5: Use historical matched atomic/480 intervention to test LS/VND sensitivity. Do not equate request caps with time or new tabu move windows.

compute_limit: 12 concurrent local workers; planned original400 trajectories72000branches, second final400 trajectories12000branches plus development/validation3600branches. Stop corrupted runs; collect complete grids, record runtime. No CPU-time truncation of valid cell selected by reward.
preregistration_boundary: Local timestamp/hash freeze, not externally timestamped preregistration. Historical48 andSAFE16 are exposed; new synthetic family is familiar even though exact32 content hashes are new.
